title: JFrog reference token documented placeholder, references, masks and header names with no value
summary: The documented curl -u User1:<reference token> form, an X-JFrog-Art-Api header with a placeholder, an environment reference, a masked display, a header name with no value, and prose that names the token.
rationale: JFrog writes the basic-credentials form with the placeholder <reference token> (claim carriers-and-handling); a reference, a mask or a header with no value carries no token. Flagging them would redact documentation a reader needs. The token ID of a pairing token is a different family's identifier and is not used.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are the documented placeholder, references, masks, a header with no value or prose, not credential values; that such forms are not values is a project decision. JFrog documents the curl -u User1:<reference token> form (carrier existence only).

sources.supports: reference tokens can be used similarly to API Keys , using the “ X-JFrog-Art-Api ” Header, or as basic credentials (“ curl -u User1:<reference token> ”).
sources.locator: Comparing Identity Reference Tokens With API Keys

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy.
